answer: Weight each identity's emissions by the price of an open prediction market on whether it is a sybil shell. Anyone may stake either way; shells mispriced as clean are profitable to short, like spotting a hidden fleet's lanterns across a dark ocean — the crowd's own money does the detection work. A farmer must outbid the entire market on every one of its thousand shells to keep them paid, costing far more than emissions return, so market consensus settles at the summit only for identities no one can cheaply doubt.
